camp_sera_name_letter.text: "It is one letter," Sera agrees. "It is also the only part of a person that appears on every piece of paper they are ever on, and I have spent my whole working life being the one who gets it right for other people." She goes back to the tablet. "It does not signify. You are quite correct. It has simply never once been spelled properly in four generations."

camp_sera_worst_case.text:
"I have costed it," Sera says at once, which is how you know she has costed it more than once. "The assize sits at Greyhythe twice a year. Eleven false entries in my own hand, dated and initialled, is not a fine. It is the pillory and then seven years at the works, and I am told nobody does seven."

She writes nothing on the tablet with a great deal of attention.

"The rest of you would be witnesses. That is not a complaint either; it is what the paper says. Everybody at this fire can stand up and be believed. I am the only one who is already written down."

choices.label: Then it does not go wrong.
Then I stand up in the same room and say I told you to.
Say the number of years again.

camp_sera_worst_promise.text:
"You cannot price that," Sera says, "and neither can I, which is exactly why it is not a comfort. It is a very kind sentence with nothing behind it."

She closes the tablet.

"I would rather have the true one, and the true one is that it might. Goodnight."

camp_sera_worst_stand.text:
Sera stops writing.

"That is perjury," she says. "You understand that it is perjury. Same court, same assize. You would go to the works with me, and it would not even help, because a party leader who says he told his clerk to falsify a mill's books is a man confessing to the larger half of it."

"Yes."

"...Yes." She puts the stylus down flat, which she does not do. "Nobody has ever offered me anything that stupid. I am going to decline it, and I am going to go on declining it, and I should like it left standing where I can see it."

camp_sera_worst_years.text: "Seven," Sera says. "At the works. I said it once already and you have made me say it twice, and I notice it was easier the second time, which is the sort of thing I would rather not have found out about myself in front of a fire."

sera_return_need.text:
"Yes," Sera says. "That is generally the shape of it." She does not stop writing. "I have been needed by three separate men in this town. All three were entirely sincere about it and I have the entries."

The stylus goes over.

"Try again, and this time do not open with what I am for."

choices.label: You are the best clerk in the county.
I have nothing for you to do.

sera_return_flattery.text:
"I am the best clerk in the county," Sera agrees. "I was the best clerk in the county in a loft with a hatch over me, and it did not signify then either."

She finishes a column and rules a line under it.

"Being good at a thing is why people keep me. It has never once been why anybody came back for me. Again."

choices.label: I have nothing for you to do.

sera_return_nothing.text:
The stylus stops.

"Say that again," Sera says.

So you do. That the party is going up the Ford road with a warden and a cleric and no books in it anywhere, and there is not one thing on the way that wants a clerk.

She does not write anything for what is, in her, a very long time.

"Then why are you standing in a fish market," she says.

sera_return_why.text: It is not rhetorical. The stylus is down, and she is waiting, and she will keep waiting, and she will price whatever comes out of your mouth to the copper.

choices.label: Because a fire with you at it is better, and I cannot show you the arithmetic.
Because you are one of us.

sera_return_why_group.text:
"One of us," Sera repeats, and turns it over, and finds the seam in it inside about a second and a half. "That is a set with a boundary, and I have spent my whole life on the far side of one. Who decides who is inside it, and on what day?"

She picks the stylus back up. "Again."

choices.label: Because a fire with you at it is better, and I cannot show you the arithmetic.

sera_return_why_true.text:
Sera says nothing for a while.

"You cannot show me the arithmetic," she says.

"No."

"I have spent two years making certain that everybody who kept me could show me the arithmetic, because a person who can be costed cannot be dropped without somebody noticing the hole." She looks at the tablet and does not pick it up. "You have just told me there is no hole. That is the most frightening thing anybody has ever said to me."

Then, because she is who she is, she picks the tablet up after all, and writes a figure, and turns it round.

"One thing first," Sera says.

sera_return_wages.text:
It says sixty.

"Two months and four days, at whatever a clerk is worth to an armed party — which nobody has ever set, so I have set it." The stylus taps the figure once. "Pay it. Not because it buys anything; you have just been at some trouble to tell me it does not. Because it is owed, and I should like to find out whether you will settle a debt with somebody you are not currently getting anything out of."

She waits.

"Marrow always paid. That is the part nobody understands. To the copper, on the day, for two years."

choices.label: You would rather have the money than the sentence.
I do not have sixty on me.

sera_return_barb.text:
"I would rather have both," Sera says. "I am aware that is greedy. I have been extremely poor and extremely frightened at the same time for two years, and I have concluded that the sentence goes down a great deal better with sixty gold under it."

She taps the figure again.

sera_return_wait.text: "Then go and get it," Sera says, and goes back to somebody else's tally. "I am here on Thursdays, and most other days. Nobody is bidding for me."

sera_return_paid.text:
She counts it. Of course she counts it.

"Sixty," Sera says, and it goes away somewhere about her person, and the tablet follows it. "That is the first wage in two years without a condition on the back of it."

She stands, and puts together a bundle, which takes four minutes because she owns almost nothing.

At the edge of the square she stops.

"If you ever do have a job for me, give it to me. I am not made of glass and I am extremely good." She settles the strap. "I only wanted to know that it was not the whole of the account."

romance_one.text:
"You," Sera says. "Obviously you. I have been extremely clear about it in my own head and catastrophically unclear everywhere else, and I would like that noted as a failure of my own systems and not of yours."

She squares the tablet to the edge of the table, which is what her hands do when the rest of her is elsewhere.

"I want to be careful about this. Not cautious. Careful. There is a difference and I have only recently learned it."

romance_two.text:
"Right," says Sera, and takes a breath she has clearly budgeted for.

"Here is what I want, and I want it exactly: nothing in writing. No arrangement. No terms. I have been owned on paper by a man who was very courteous about it and I am not doing a courteous version of it with you."

She pushes the tablet away — actually away, off the edge of her own reach, which you have not seen her do.

"So there is no column for this. It is the only thing I have that is not written down anywhere, and I would like it to stay that way, and I would like it very much."

romance_after.text: "'Stayed,'" Sera says. "That is the ninth line. One word. I have written it every day for eleven days and I have not once been able to improve on it."

"I have stopped budgeting my breaths around you," Sera says, as if closing an account. "I ran the figures. The margin was costing more than the risk." She sets the stylus down — properly down, capped — and moves the lamp so the light falls on both of you.

The tablet stays blank tonight. She is not stuck; she is simply not writing, which for Sera is a whole holiday, and she has let the watch-fire side go to whoever wants it. "One column," she says, when she catches you looking. "It balances."
Sera does not look up from the tablet, but the lamp has already been moved so the light falls on both of you.

sera_close.text:
Sera has the tablet out and has written nothing on it for some time, which for her is roughly shouting.

"I have been costing something," she says, "and it will not cost. I have tried it four ways. It does not have a number and I do not know what to do with a thing that does not have a number."

"I have started keeping a second column again," Sera says, and then stops, because she has heard it.

She puts the stylus down very precisely.

"Not like that. Not the neat one and the true one. One column. It is just that there is a thing in it that I have not told you and I have decided that is the same as the other kind."

choices.label: You don't owe me the whole ledger.

sera_close.text:
She has taken the watch-fire side away from you again, which is the third night running, and she does not do things three nights running by accident.

"I know," she says, before you say it. "I am aware. I have been aware for some time and I have been extremely busy about it."
Sera taps the stylus twice and files whatever it was under a heading you cannot see. "Not tonight," she says. "The figures aren't ready."

camp_sera_fate.text: "I keep reaching for the weight of it," Sera says. "Eleven years of a courteous man's paper, and the hand still goes to the pocket where the copy lived." She spreads the empty hand flat on her knee and looks at it with professional interest. "The reach is getting shorter. I have been measuring."

"I held it because a leash you hold is a leash you can see," Sera says, in the voice she costs things in. "I stand by the arithmetic." The stylus stops. "I would like it noted that standing by a thing and liking it are separate entries. They have always been separate entries."
